messages:
sara: heads up — OrionPay on dedicated pool is seeing lots of tiny batches and p95 spikes after the last model rollout. they asked if we can tweak their token budget / queue limits.
miguel: can you paste the profiling traces you have? curious if KV cache evictions are involved or if kernel fallback is the culprit.
sara: pasted key bits below from local profiler (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] trace=req-83421
model_variant: rdx-13b-q4f
avg_seq: 48 tokens, tail_seq: 1024 tokens
kernel_select: aten_gemm fallback (12% of tokens), fast_attn kernels used otherwise
kv_cache_evictions: 18/min (working set ~1.6GB)
batch_formation: median batch_size=3, mean wait=42ms
p95_latency: 420ms (baseline 180ms)
```

jonah: wow. that GEMM fallback for long tails explains the per-token spike. small batches + occasional long seqs -> kernel selector switches and loses throughput.
tess: OrionPay workload is chatty — lots of short requests interspersed with long history restores. their current per-request token_budget is 4096 and queue_limit is 256, right?
sara: current config on their Dedicated pool: token_budget_per_req=4096, queue_limit=256, allow_long_tail=true
miguel: two levers to try: 1) lower per-request token_budget to encourage earlier truncation (if acceptable), 2) tighten queue_limit to force aggregation control and reduce tiny-batch tail noise. also we can bias kernel selector to prefer fast_attn for mixed-length batches (soft preference) while we investigate kernel perf regression.
jonah: preference sounds risky but ok as a short canary. for OrionPay I'd propose: token_budget_per_req=2048, queue_limit=128, max_queued_tokens=512k (global pool cap). that should reduce kv working set and eviction churn.
sara: OrionPay support says they can tolerate some truncation for now if p95 improves. they want a conservative change first.
ci-bot: alert: canary rollout to dedicated pool orion-01 scheduled in 10m. config delta: {"token_budget_per_req":2048, "queue_limit":128, "max_queued_tokens":524288}
miguel: also add a KV retention tweak: keep_recent_prefix=128 and aggressive_prefix_eviction=false — prevents losing the small-window histories that drive short requests.
ops-bot: note: will enforce per-customer queue limits at the tokenflow layer; if queue_limit hit, requests will be rejected with 429 and header X-Queue-Reason: limit-exceeded
tess: one more idea: enable prefix-aware batching for this pool so requests that share a prefix (same convo id) are fastpath'd into KV-cache-friendly batches.
jonah: +1. Instrumentation needed: token budget acceptance rate, 429 rate, avg batch_size, kv_evictions/min. Can we add those metrics to their dashboard?
sara: I'll open a dashboard PR and assign grafana panels to orionpay team. also adding a perf probe to capture kernel_select ratios per-minute.
miguel: after 24h canary, if p95 drops ~30% and 429s <1%, we can keep changes. if KV evictions still >10/min we'll fallback token_budget->1024 and revisit kernel selector tuning.
jonah: agreed. if we still see gemm fallback, we need to capture a minimal repro and escalate to runtime-kernels.
sara: OrionPay notified, they approved canary. deploying now.
ci-bot: deploy started: canary config applied to orion-01 at 1773321723 by sara
sara: keeping thread open for early signals, will post dashboard link once PR merges. :eyes:
